rationale: Evidence: the iteration 7 build (kd 0.8, kp 3.5) is the best raced design at 304.77. Its oval finishes 13 of 20 (mean finish 1.90 s), but the s-bend (progress 0.30) and slalom (progress 0.19) still end off track with steering_oscillation of 0.23 and 0.25. The kp 3.0 test (iteration 8) dropped the score to 296.66 without clearing the bends, so kp is not the lever to push. Earlier steps showed that raising kd (0.3 to 0.5 to 0.8) cut oscillation and produced the only large gains. Change: controller.kd 0.8 to 1.0, with kp 3.5, sensor y 0.07, x -0.04 to +0.04, sensor_size 0.012, base_speed 1.6, line_loss last_direction and geometry all unchanged. This is a single-variable test of more damping on the bends. Expected result: steering_oscillation on the s-bend and slalom falls below about 0.23, progress on those tracks rises above 0.30 and 0.19, and the oval keeps at least 13 of 20 finishes, for a score at or above 304.77. Fallback: if the score is below 304.77 or oval finishes fall below 13 of 20, the derivative is past its useful range, so the Evaluator should approve the iteration 7 build (kd 0.8, kp 3.5). Hypotheses: (H1) more kd damps the overshoot that drives the bend line losses; (H2) if oscillation rises further, the derivative is amplifying sensor noise and kd should stay near 0.8; (H3) if the bends still fail with lower oscillation, the next lever is base_speed (lower for bend overshoot), not gain. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and controller_errors on all three tracks.
